def: A fitted formula giving a model's loss as a function of its parameters and training tokens.
The 70-billion-parameter model and paper (Hoffmann et al., 2022) showing that model size and training tokens should scale together.
The split of a compute budget between model size and data that gives the lowest loss.
The approximation that training a Transformer costs about 6 floating-point operations per parameter per token.
The floor E in the scaling law that no amount of parameters or data removes.
A rule for scaling initial values and learning rates with width so that updates change each layer's output by a width-independent amount.
Tuning hyperparameters on a small model parametrised in μP and copying them to a large one without tuning it directly.
Predicting a value outside the range of the data a model was fitted on, such as the loss of a much larger model.
A METR task that asks for the best model shape at 5e17 FLOPs using only experiments of 1e16 FLOPs or less.
